subject: Air-gapped deployment: egress budget, latency & streaming concurrency — post-call actions
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@edgescale.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: air-gapped deployment constraints and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side based on the call: 

Summary of constraints you shared
- Air-gapped (no outbound internet) for model payloads and inference RPCs; control-plane access allowed via restricted bastion with exact IP allowlist.
- Egress must be via customer-controlled relay (we'll talk through a secure forwarder/proxy pattern).
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 80ms for streaming chat turn completions at 512 tokens.
- Expected concurrency: 60 concurrent streaming sessions during peak; burst to 120 for 3–5 minutes acceptable.

Open questions we still have
1) Can the bastion perform TLS termination for the control plane, or only TCP forwarding?
2) Are there software-stack constraints for installing our lightweight agent (we discussed containerized vs systemd)?
3) Do you have a rough egress bandwidth ceiling (Mbps) for the on-prem relay during peak?

Proposed next steps
- Action A (EdgeScale): share a sample allowlist and the bastion's packet flow diagram — due Thu Jul 1 EOD.
- Action B (Redwood): produce a short runbook and recommended proxy topology for air-gapped inference (attached redwood-mini-runbook.pdf) — target Fri Jul 2.
- Action C (Joint): schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive with your infra + our runtime team; suggested slots Mon Jul 5 or Tue Jul 6.

I've attached a skeleton SLO worksheet (slo-proposal-edgescale.xlsx) and a small packet-capture we captured during our demo to illustrate typical streaming handshake behavior (network-trace-20270630.pcap).

If the above matches your understanding, reply with approval and preferred slot for the deep-dive.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: air-gapped deployment constraints and next steps

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap. Couple answers inline and a couple items from our side: 

Inline answers
- Bastion: currently only TCP forwarding (no TLS termination). We can consider upgrading but that's a 2–3 week change.
- Agent install: containerized only (we cannot run additional system services). Agent must run as non-root.
- Egress bandwidth: baseline 200 Mbps, can be elevated to 400 Mbps for brief bursts if pre-notified.

EdgeScale deliverables
- We'll send an allowlist + flow diagram by EOD Fri Jul 2.
- Infra team requests an example of the control-plane handshake logs we expect to see so they can map to existing logging.

Deep-dive timing: Jul 6 at 11:00am PT works best for our infra folks.

— Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Infrastructure | EdgeScale Inc.
alex.rivera@edgescale.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: air-gapped deployment constraints and next steps

Alex / team — Marcus from the runtime team here. Quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so we can be concrete on the call:

Runtime assumptions for the proposed setup
- Streaming model: we assume HTTP/2-based chunked streaming over a mutually authenticated TLS channel when possible; given your bastion is TCP-forward-only, we'll show a tunnel proxy pattern that preserves HTTP/2 in the interior network.
- Latency testing plan: we'll run a synthetic harness with 512-token responses and measure tail latency on your relay. Expect to instrument both client-side (EdgeScale) and server-side (Redwood) latencies to isolate network vs kernel processing.
- Concurrency handling: our serving runtime will keep ~8 worker shards per GPU for the model family you specified; with your concurrency target (60) we estimate 2 x A100-class GPUs dedicated with headroom for burst. We'll surface more precise numbers after we see sample QPS and token-per-request distributions.

Pre-call ask (please bring to the deep-dive)
1) A packet capture focused on a 60–90 second high-concurrency window, if available. The sample you sent was helpful; a live capture during peak would be ideal.
2) Confirmation that the relay will preserve source IP or provide an X-Forwarded-For header to help with request routing.

I'll prepare a short slide (1–2) to outline the tunnel/proxy variants and our recommended measurements. See attached 'network-trace-20270630.pcap' for the example flow.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Thanks Marcus — this is exactly the kind of prep we wanted. A few quick confirmations before the deep-dive: 

- We can provide a 90s packet capture from our planned maintenance window; IT will redact internal hostnames but keep IPs. ETA: Jul 5 10:00am PT.
- Relay will add X-Forwarded-For header; preserving source IP directly is harder because of NAT in our environment.
- We'll circulate the bastion TCP-flow diagram and allowlist by EOD today.

See you Jul 6 at 11:00am PT. Please include a calendar invite with a dial-in and our preferred internal room (EdgeScale-RD1).

— Alex
